races.name: British Stallion Studs EBF Fillies' Restricted Novice Stakes (For Horses In Bands C And D) (GBB Race)
When You Wish Upon A Star Race Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Al Sayah
runners_data.note: Six-year-old front-runner with a recent win at 2m over good ground and strong similar-going form (5W9P in 15 runs), wearing a visor; uncontested lead is the key asset here, though Ashley Lewis's 5lb claim is worth noting on a horse that needs to be ridden positively.|
runners_data.comment: Third last time out, and a winner three starts back, Al Sayah has already raced over today's trip and returns after 53 days off. Two blank runs sit earlier in the profile, but she ranks second on our figures and looks the leading threat.

runners_data.name: Merrijig
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up type who finished second over 2m on good ground 17 days ago — trip and conditions suit well — and trainer John Berry has a live 1/3 in the 14-day window; blinkered, so likely to stay focused at the back of this small field.|
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out, Merrijig arrives in good form and has already proven he stays today's trip. A win four starts back underlines the ability, and with a quick 17-day turnaround and the top spot on our figures, he's the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Simiyann
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare whose recent form shows a win and a placed effort but is surrounded by modest figures on similar going (7/15); the 3lb claim from Kavanagh helps at a big weight pull, but her distance record at 2m+ is limited and the step up from 2m is a question mark.|
runners_data.comment: Fourth last time out, following two blank efforts and a sixth further back, Simiyann is yet to win in recent starts but already has today's trip covered and returns quickly after 17 days. He ranks third on our figures among the leading dangers.

runners_data.name: Regally Blonde
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer by nature — pace mapping places her in midfield only because the field is loaded with closers — so her actual race position will likely be further back than the map suggests; padded tongue-tie in play and trainer Ben Case has a quiet recent strike rate (0/3 in 14 days).|
runners_data.comment: Third last time out and race-fit again after just 13 days, Regally Blonde is yet to score in recent starts but that finish hints at ability. Modest efforts before it leave her fourth-best on our figures, with more needed to trouble the front two.

runners_data.name: Oceanides
runners_data.note: A true closer by style whose midfield mapping reflects redistribution rather than intent, so expect her to race from the rear; at four she is the youngest in the field, stepping up significantly from 10-12f to 2m2f, and her form on anything resembling good ground is thin (1/6 in similar conditions) — trip and going are both genuine queries.|
runners_data.comment: A well-held sixth last time out and without a win in recent starts, Oceanides has found the frame elusive, with two runs further back again before that. Fit after 17 days off, she's rated bottom of this field on our figures.

races.paceDynamic: Al Sayah is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-horse field over 2m2f at Nottingham, and with no genuine pace rival to challenge him, he should be permitted to dictate a controlled, sustainable tempo from the outset. The three hold-up types — Merrijig, Simiyann, and the two redistributed midfielders Regally Blonde and Oceanides — will track at a respectful distance, meaning the race is likely to develop as a steady-pace procession until the final turn shakes things loose. Crucially, Regally Blonde and Oceanides are true hold-up horses pushed into mapped midfield positions because the field contains more closers than the shape can accommodate at the rear, so neither is likely to actually sit that prominently; their natural home is off the pace. This shape overwhelmingly favours hold-up horses with a powerful late finish, as Al Sayah's uncontested lead sets a tempo that should leave plenty in the tank for one genuine stayer to sweep past late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Al Sayah Controls, Closers Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Al Sayah dictates a steady, uncontested tempo and the race develops into a one-paced slog over the final half-mile.
scenarios.body: Al Sayah rolls along at his own pace with nothing to challenge him early, conserving enough energy to be competitive entering the straight, while one or two of the hold-up horses produce a measured late run on the good ground. Merrijig and Simiyann, both confirmed hold-up types with solid form on good going, are best placed to benefit from this controlled-pace scenario.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Al Sayah sets an overly dawdling early gallop and the race becomes a sprint finish off a crawl.
scenarios.body: A near-stationary early pace turns the race into a tactical affair, with the field bunched heading into the straight and jockeys forced to make their moves earlier than ideal. In this scenario Merrijig's experienced handler and Jason Watson's tactical nous give them an edge, while Simiyann risks being outpaced by a sudden injection of speed.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Al Sayah Steals It Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Al Sayah's uncontested lead allows him to build a significant advantage that the hold-up horses cannot reel in from a standing start.
scenarios.body: With a generous OR drop and a visor working in his favour, Al Sayah builds an unchallenged lead at a pace just quick enough to stretch the field without burning himself out, and the hold-up horses simply run out of ground in the straight. His recent win at this trip on good ground is the key form reference, and Neil Mulholland's runners have form when fresh horses are being aimed at a specific target.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Misfired
scenarios.trigger: If the redistributed horses fail to travel smoothly and the race defaults to a two-horse finish between Al Sayah and the best-placed hold-up type.
scenarios.body: Oceanides, the youngest and least experienced runner at this marathon trip, fails to settle or gets outpaced as the field strings out, leaving Regally Blonde and the backmarkers too much to do. This compressed, messy scenario suits a horse that can travel mid-pack and produce one clean burst, making Merrijig the likeliest beneficiary given his recent course-relevant form.

watchPoints.text: Al Sayah is completely alone on the front end — if he is allowed to bowl along unchallenged at a sensible tempo for this trip, his lead could prove very difficult to pull back over 2m2f with only four horses in pursuit.

Merrijig's last two runs have both been on good or good-to-firm going over shorter trips; watch whether Jason Watson commits early or waits, as the hold-up play relies on a strong enough gallop to run into.

Oceanides has never raced beyond 12f and has produced no wins or places on comparable going — if the pace is steady she could be outpaced in the straight before her hold-up style can deliver any impact.

With four hold-up horses in a five-runner field, watch for a crowded finish entering the straight — multiple horses making their runs simultaneously could cause interference or result in one of them getting squeezed for a run.

The going report is listed as unknown throughout, so monitor any late ground update before the race — Al Sayah's form on soft going is considerably weaker, and a change in conditions could materially alter the pace dynamic.|

races.name: XMA Wish Race "Confined" Handicap Stakes (For Horses Who Have Not Won More Than One Race)

runners_data.name: Black Missile
runners_data.note: Julie Camacho's three-year-old has shown ability but only one piece of good-going form in five runs (sim-going 1/5), and as a genuine hold-up horse pushed into a midfield slot here, it faces a positional compromise that will blunt its chance unless the pace truly collapses.|
runners_data.comment: Fifth in each of his last two starts, following a pair of fourths and a third further back, Black Missile already has today's trip covered and is fresh again after 50 days off. He's second on our figures, making him one of the leading dangers despite that recent dip in form.

runners_data.name: Rousham
runners_data.note: Nigel Tinkler's runner has winning and placed form on good ground over this trip and, although it is a natural hold-up type, its tactical versatility makes it one of the more likely candidates to actually secure a close-tracking position in this pace-starved field.|
runners_data.comment: Fourth last time out having been unplaced the run before, Rousham won three starts back, and was runner-up the one before that, showing there's ability. He already goes well over today's trip and is fresh after 22 days, but sits only fifth-best of seven on our figures — a fair yet unremarkable profile.

runners_data.name: Liquid Cooled
runners_data.note: Ben Haslam's charge returns after 82 days off and has only one piece of comparable going form in six runs; it is by inclination a hold-up horse that will find itself occupying a midfield berth it didn't choose, and the layoff adds another layer of doubt.|
runners_data.comment: Third last time out, and a winner three starts back, Liquid Cooled does have redeeming recent form, though a run of 82 days without a race is a concern fitness-wise. He already goes well over today's trip, but sits bottom on our figures, making a bold showing hard to expect.

runners_data.name: Slot
runners_data.note: Antony Brittain's runner is the sole confirmed pace-setter and will enjoy an uncontested lead — the style-fit score of 0.93 reflects a horse that is only a moderate rather than dominant front-runner, but here unchallenged that may be good enough.|
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out and never worse than fifth in her other recent starts, Slot has been freshened up after just 22 days and already goes well over today's trip. She's third-best on our figures, making her one of the leading dangers.

runners_data.name: Whizzy Dizzy
runners_data.note: Clive Cox supplies a three-year-old returning after 126 days, and its all-turf form is exclusively on standard-to-slow ground (five runs, sim-going 1/6); the layoff and going question are genuine concerns despite a trainer who fires returners.|
runners_data.comment: A sixth last time out leaves Whizzy Dizzy short of the placings, though she was runner-up five starts back and already goes well over today's trip. A lengthy 126-day absence is a big concern, and she's only sixth-best of seven on our figures.

runners_data.name: Robert Anstruther
runners_data.note: Henry Candy's runner has failed to win in eight starts and its seven-furlong profile means dropping to 6f here is actually a potential concern; true hold-up style but squeezed into a midfield role where it is unlikely to get the fast pace it needs to close.|
runners_data.comment: Third last time out — his best effort of the past five starts — Robert Anstruther followed three sevenths and a fourth with a clear step forward, and he's fresh again after just 18 days with today's trip already covered. He's fourth on our figures among the more solid dangers here.

runners_data.name: Night Mission
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's highest-rated runner (OR 70) carries an unknown style tag, has placed twice on good ground, and sits at the top of the weights — if it can find a handy position it is the most open-to-interpretation runner and could benefit if pace develops.|
runners_data.comment: Seventh last time out, Night Mission was runner-up four starts back, and third before that, form that puts him clear on our figures. He already goes well over today's six-furlong trip, and despite 49 days off since, he rates the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Ballybunion
runners_data.note: Michael Bell's runner has placed twice over this C&D on good ground and, while a hold-up type by inclination, is one of those most likely to secure a prominent position naturally given its course and distance familiarity; the 70-day absence is the main query.|

races.paceDynamic: Slot is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no other genuine pace horse to push it along, is set to bowl along in front at a controlled, sustainable tempo over this 6f on good turf at Nottingham. The field is loaded with hold-up types — Black Missile, Rousham, Liquid Cooled, Robert Anstruther and Ballybunion all prefer to race off the pace — but the map cannot place them all at the rear; several will be shuffled into midfield positions against their natural inclinations. This field holds more hold-up types than can genuinely get to the back of the field, with Rousham and Ballybunion the most likely to actually secure a prominent tracking position given their recent course and distance evidence, while the others will be forced wider and higher than ideal. A modest, controlled pace set by Slot strongly favours horses who can track closely and pounce in the straight — prominent racers or those who can sit just off the leader — rather than pure closers who need a fast pace to reel in.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Slot Controls, Closers Late
scenarios.trigger: If Slot sets a comfortable solo lead and holds enough tempo to string the field out before fading in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Slot dictates from the front at a sustainable clip, compressing the field as closers get a sensible target to aim at in the final two furlongs; horses who can track in second or third — like Rousham or Ballybunion who may sit closer than their style suggests — are ideally placed to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Slot Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Slot's controlled pace is slow enough that it conserves enough energy to hold on all the way to the line.
scenarios.body: Slot bowls along uncontested and never expends enough energy to stop, meaning the closers arrive too late having been denied a true target pace; a front-runner winning a slowly-run sprint off a low OR is entirely plausible.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Hold-Ups Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Slot is pressed more than expected by runners shuffled forward against their nature, creating a faster pace that burns out the leaders.
scenarios.body: A slightly hotter gallop than anticipated could see the front end fold inside the final furlong, releasing hold-up types who manage to find clear air; however, because most of the true closers are redistributed and racing out of role, the benefit is muted and the outcome messy.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Muddle Decides
scenarios.trigger: If traffic problems and jostling among the large group of misplaced hold-up types create a chaotic straight, with the winner threading through late.
scenarios.body: The redistribution of so many hold-up horses into midfield creates potential for interference and blocked runs in the final two furlongs; the winner in this shape needs a clean passage and a sharp turn of foot, but the probability is low because the moderate pace does not set this up naturally.

watchPoints.text: Slot (Cam Hardie) will control the pace entirely unchallenged — watch whether it quickens or simply keeps the same tempo in the final 2f, as the outcome of the whole race hinges on that single variable.|
Rousham and Ballybunion are the two hold-up horses best-placed to track Slot more closely than their labels suggest — watch their early positioning out of the stalls as a key race-shape indicator.|
Whizzy Dizzy returns after 126 days for Clive Cox and has no relevant good-ground form; watch for any market move that might signal Haydock-style sharpness behind the scenes.|

The cluster of redistributed hold-up types (Black Missile, Robert Anstruther, Liquid Cooled) will be jostling for the same midfield ground — watch for crowding and checked runs on the turn into the straight, which could compromise several runners simultaneously.|

races.name: PKF Wish Race Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Washington Heir
runners_data.note: Landed a 6f good-ground contest 17 days ago for Tony Carroll and Jack Doughty, and his hold-up style is at least respected in a race where the back is overcrowded — he sits closest to a natural mid-division stalking spot and his sim-going record flags three placings in eight efforts on good turf.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out, having won the run before that, Washington Heir does have compact recent form, though modest efforts further back temper the picture. He already goes well over today's trip, but he's rated bottom of this field on our figures, leaving plenty to prove.

runners_data.name: Baileys Ontherocks
runners_data.note: Carroll's second string here; this horse's natural inclination is to come from the back but with so many rivals wanting the same ground, it will struggle to find its rhythm — only one placing in twelve efforts on similar going makes the case for support thin.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out, a form spike after a string of finishes no better than sixth, Baileys Ontherocks is fresh again having run just 10 days ago and already goes well over today's trip. She's seventh on our figures, so more like that placing is needed to feature.

runners_data.name: Ganthorpe
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason takes the ride on a 3-year-old with a win at 6f on good for the Easterby yard; dropping to 5f is a query but the good-ground record is solid and a hold-up style that naturally settles this horse could work if late ground materialises.
runners_data.comment: Seventh in each of his last two starts, Ganthorpe did win three starts back, but a run of modest finishes either side of that tempers the appeal. He already goes well over today's trip and is fresh after 18 days, though he's only eighth-best of nine on our figures.

runners_data.name: Jackie Brown
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner in this field and the key pace-setter, though it is worth noting that good ground is a concern — all five recent runs have been on soft or standard surfaces, and the STYLE_FIT flag highlights it may be pushed slightly further forward than ideal; Adrian Wintle's 3/11 in-form 14-day window helps.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out, with another third among her form further back, Jackie Brown has the frame within range on her better days, though a ninth in between shows she can also disappoint. She already goes well over today's trip and is fresh after 18 days, rated fifth on our figures.

runners_data.name: Rinky Tinky Tinky
runners_data.note: Forced out of its true back-of-the-field role by the volume of hold-up horses in this race; the headgear (p) did not unlock a win in seven efforts on good going and a 44-day absence adds to the uncertainty around its readiness.
runners_data.comment: Sixth last time out and yet to better a fourth in recent starts, Rinky Tinky Tinky has struggled to get into the mix, with a pair of eighths further back the low point. She already goes well over today's trip and returns after 44 days, rated only sixth-best of nine here.

runners_data.name: Sir Benedict
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old who has produced five placed efforts from fifteen good-ground starts, including two seconds at this 5f trip; Andrew Mullen rides and the horse maps honestly into a position that suits a horse wanting to travel smoothly and grind late.
runners_data.comment: Sixth last time out, Sir Benedict has otherwise been fairly consistent, with a third and a runner-up among his last six starts, and he already goes well over today's trip. Fresh again after 29 days, he's third on our figures and rates one of the leading dangers despite that recent blip.

runners_data.name: Antiphon
runners_data.note: Has finished third in five of its last fifteen outings but the fade-in-finish flag is a genuine concern over the minimum trip, and the horse's true hold-up role is compromised by field overcrowding at the back — nine good-ground runs without a win says it all.
runners_data.comment: Unplaced last time out, having been ninth the run before, Antiphon does have three thirds further back to fall on, and he already goes well over today's trip. Fresh again after just 18 days, he tops our figures in this field, but the recent dip is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Captain Kinsella
runners_data.note: A 123-day layoff is the headline concern; the horse prefers a standard surface based on its entire recent form and has no wins or places from four efforts on good going, so it arrives rusty and on unfavoured ground.
runners_data.comment: Fifth last time out, and fourth the run before, Captain Kinsella found form in his last two starts after three modest efforts, and he already has today's trip covered. A 123-day gap since is a concern, but that upturn makes him our narrow pick ahead of the highest-rated runner here.

runners_data.name: Desert Master
runners_data.note: Two seconds on good ground in recent form — including a 2nd over this 5f trip — give this Antony Brittain-trained 5-year-old legitimate claims, and Cam Hardie's booking adds purpose; the visor headgear is retained and it has shown the ability to finish fast enough on similar going to be competitive even from a redistributed position.
runners_data.comment: Seventh last time out, Desert Master has been freshened up after just 16 days, but there's solid form in this book too — a fourth and two runner-up efforts among his last six starts. He already goes well over today's trip and ranks fourth on our figures among the leading dangers.

races.paceDynamic: Jackie Brown is the sole confirmed front-runner and should lead from the outset at a sustainable, uncontested gallop over this 5f on good turf at Nottingham. With no rival likely to seriously dispute the lead, Jackie Brown can control tempo from the front and potentially produce a flat, even-paced affair rather than a true end-to-end test. The field behind is overwhelmingly populated by hold-up horses — Baileys Ontherocks, Antiphon, Captain Kinsella, Rinky Tinky Tinky, and Desert Master are all genuine hold-up types redistributed into midfield slots because there simply is not enough room at the back for all of them to operate naturally. This race shape, with one unhurried pace-setter and a wall of closers competing for ground late, strongly favours the horse with the best tactical awareness from a prominent or stalking position, particularly Washington Heir, Ganthorpe, and Sir Benedict, who can sit closest to the pace without being pushed out of their preferred roles.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Jackie Brown Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Jackie Brown secures a clean lead and is allowed to regulate a comfortable, unforced tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: Jackie Brown sets an honest but controlled gallop and the hold-up horses fail to generate enough closing momentum against a pace that is never truly fast; the horse that tracks closest and travels smoothly into the straight reaps the reward.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse travelling just off the leader's quarters quickens sharply when Jackie Brown is done in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The controlled pace suits a prominent tracker who is saving energy through the race and can sprint past a tiring leader; Washington Heir's good-ground record and Sir Benedict's consistent placed form over 5f on similar surfaces make them the profiles to thrive here.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Finish Fast
scenarios.trigger: If Jackie Brown sets a genuinely strong early clip that burns off rivals and leaves the closing ground opening up in the final 100 yards.
scenarios.body: A pace collapse late could allow the redistributed hold-up horses to pick up the pieces, but most of them are racing away from their natural position and are unlikely to produce a true flying finish; Desert Master and Ganthorpe have the best recent good-ground evidence among the closers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse — Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so moderate that the race turns into a sprint for home with no meaningful separation until the last 100 yards.
scenarios.body: In a muddled finish where positional advantage counts for little, any of the redistributed midfield horses could stumble into a place, but the lack of genuine pace and uncertain going reports make this the least structured and least predictable shape.

watchPoints.text: Jackie Brown is the sole pace-setter and if it gets a clean lead, the entire race shape pivots around whether it can sustain that gallop to the line — any early bump or rival upsetting its jump could fundamentally alter the tempo.

The going is listed as unknown at Nottingham across all reports — if conditions are softer than anticipated, horses with soft-ground form such as Jackie Brown and Ganthorpe may be advantaged while good-ground specialists face an unexpected test.

Captain Kinsella returns after a 123-day absence with a record of zero wins or places from four runs on good going — watch in-running for it to drop out quickly if the surface and freshness combine badly.

Antiphon is flagged as fading in the finish and races off its preferred extreme hold-up position; if it is seen travelling well into the straight but stopping, that is relevant form evidence for future races rather than a winning move today.

Desert Master has the most compelling recent good-ground evidence among the redistributed hold-up horses — two seconds including over 5f — and Cam Hardie's booking suggests connections expect a forward showing despite the positional compromise.

races.name: Arthur Johnson & Sons Wish Race "Confined" Handicap Stakes (For Horses Which Have Not Won A Race In 2026)

runners_data.name: Goldie Trickett
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer for Jane Chapple-Hyam whose best form at 8f on good or standard suggests the 10f here stretches her stamina; Callum Hutchinson takes the ride on a 34-day turnaround and her sim-going record (0W0P) gives little encouragement, though she placed last time out.
runners_data.comment: Fourth last time out and yet to win in recent starts, Goldie Trickett already has today's trip covered and returns after 34 days off. A third four starts back remains the pick of her form, and she's third-best on our figures among the leading dangers.

runners_data.name: Token Love
runners_data.note: Showed a placed effort over 10f on standard ground and represents Micky Hammond on a 79-day absence; the tongue-tie is retained, but the lengthy lay-off and a 0/9 record on similar going are both flags, and her natural style means she needs a true pace to run at which this field simply cannot provide.
runners_data.comment: Fourth last time out, Token Love is yet to win in recent starts but did finish runner-up four starts back and already goes well over today's trip. A gap of 79 days since is the obvious query, but he's fourth on our figures and can't be ruled out among the dangers.

runners_data.name: Revich
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old veteran with a consistent good-ground profile (5 of last 15 runs on similar going) for Adrian Wintle, returned to form with a placed effort 34 days ago; his true style is hold-up but the absence of any leader means he is the horse most likely to fill the pace vacuum, and if he does that suits him better than sitting and waiting — STYLE_FIT tempers his claim in a pure hold-up shape.
runners_data.comment: Fourth last time out, following a third two runs back and three sixths among his other starts, Revich is without a win in recent starts but already goes well over today's trip. He's fresh again after just 34 days and ranks second on our figures as the leading threat.

runners_data.name: Finally Escaped
runners_data.note: Roger Fell's four-year-old has a modest form string of 265664 and only 2 qualifying runs on similar going; 84 days off the track is a concern in a race that may demand tactical sharpness, and while he is a natural hold-up type his STYLE_FIT tag reflects that he may find himself racing more prominently than ideal.
runners_data.comment: Fourth last time out, Finally Escaped has today's trip already covered and the deeper form in this sequence includes a runner-up effort further back. An 84-day absence is the one query, but she tops our figures by a wide margin and rates the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Brouhaha
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's three-year-old has run three times, all finishing last, but arrives here on just a 16-day turnaround which gives him a significant fitness edge over several rivals; his natural style is hold-up but in a field devoid of pace he may press forward, and Alistair Rawlinson's claim could prove useful in a race likely to be won from a forward position.
runners_data.comment: Three straight sixths and no better than that in recent starts leave Brouhaha hard to fancy on figures, though he is fresh having run just 16 days ago. He's fifth-best of six on our numbers, and marked improvement is needed to get involved in this.

runners_data.name: Nicolai
runners_data.note: Neil Mulholland's three-year-old carries a ⚠ fade-in-finish flag and a form string of 8-8860 on mostly standard ground; a 99-day absence is the longest in the field and his entire profile points away from this race — out of form, likely to struggle for fitness, and his tendency to weaken late is a serious negative in a sprint-finish scenario.
runners_data.comment: A modest recent record of one unplaced effort and a string of finishes no better than sixth leave Nicolai hard to fancy, and a 99-day layoff adds to the concerns. He's the bottom-rated runner on our figures, so a bold showing would be a surprise.

races.paceDynamic: With every single runner in this six-horse field carrying a hold-up profile, there is no natural front-runner and no horse inclined to press on from the gates — the race will almost certainly crawl into the straight before erupting into a sprint finish over the final two furlongs. Goldie Trickett and Token Love are the two genuine hold-up types at the rear, while Revich, Finally Escaped, Brouhaha and Nicolai are all true hold-up horses redistributed into a midfield mapping because the field contains far more closers than the race shape can accommodate. The field holds more hold-up types than can all get their position; of those redistributed, Revich's proven good-ground form and Brouhaha's recency make them the most likely to press forward into a more prominent berth in the absence of any natural leader. The absence of any pace means this race will favour the horse with the best finishing kick from a prominent position once the sprint ignites — a horse that can travel handily in the tactical vacuum and produce a sustained effort into the Nottingham straight holds the key advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sprint Finish From Midfield
scenarios.trigger: If the field crawls early and the race becomes a two-furlong dash, forcing a positional scramble
scenarios.body: With no pace to run at, the entire field bunches and the race is decided on raw sprint ability from wherever horses can get to on the home turn; a horse able to sit handy in the tactical vacuum and produce a sharp, sustained kick holds the advantage here.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Revich Dictates From Front
scenarios.trigger: If Revich or Brouhaha press on unopposed and set a modest but genuine gallop that never quickens sufficiently to flush out the closers
scenarios.body: One of the redistributed hold-up types drifts forward to fill the vacuum and sets a steady tempo, meaning the race is run at their pace and they control the fractions into the straight; a horse with tactical versatility and good-ground form benefits most in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Swooper Lands Blow
scenarios.trigger: If a genuine mid-race injection of pace by one horse strings the field out and creates a real target for late challengers
scenarios.body: A stronger-than-expected gallop burns off the tactical types and leaves the race open for a horse switching off at the back and unleashing a late run; Goldie Trickett and Token Love, both true hold-up runners with some good-ground form, are best placed to benefit.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Attrition Grinds Them Down
scenarios.trigger: If the lack of pace combined with the 1m2f trip catches out the less exposed or less fit horses on their first run back after a long break
scenarios.body: The stop-start nature of a race with no pace can be surprisingly taxing on horses returning from long absences such as Token Love (79 days) and Finally Escaped (84 days), and a horse with recent racecourse fitness like Brouhaha (16 days) picks up the pieces.

watchPoints.text: Revich and Brouhaha are the most likely to press forward into the pace vacuum — watch the early exchanges to see which, if either, takes a lead, as the horse who controls the modest fractions from the front could dictate the result.

Token Love (79 days) and Finally Escaped (84 days) are both returning from extended absences in a race where there is no honest gallop to get them into their rhythm — monitor their early movement for any signs of ring-rustiness.

Nicolai's fade-in-finish flag combined with a 99-day break and a record of finishing last in all three starts makes him a horse to watch only as a market indicator — if backed, it suggests stable confidence that is hard to reconcile with the form.

Goldie Trickett's jockey Callum Hutchinson will need to make a forward move on the home turn given the lack of pace; watch whether she is in a position to challenge entering the straight or still waiting for gaps that may not materialise.

The going is listed as unknown across all six runners — any last-minute going update before racing could alter the tactical picture, particularly for horses like Revich whose profile is clearly tied to good ground.
